messages.author: a9bd4cb1ebe5e5f2
messages.subject: Goodness of fit statistics
parts:
Hello blavaan community,

First-time poster, so first let me say thank you for such an excellent piece of software!

Are there ways to compute analogous fit statistics to those which are commonly reported in frequentist SEM, like CFI, RMSEA or Chi^2? I personally don't like to put much emphasis on fit statistics other than predictive validity, but I know that "traditional" SEM people (potential reviewers) might. Are BIC, DIC and WAIC the only options at my disposal if I use blavaan?

Reference: http://davidakenny.net/cm/fit.htm

Thanks,
David

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Goodness of fit statistics
parts:
Hi David,

A metric somewhat similar to the chi-squared statistic is there, labeled as the posterior predictive p-value "ppp". Some further info on this is discussed in the appendix of the blavaan paper:

http://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05604

The others (RMSEA, CFI, etc) are simple to compute, but I'm not quite sure what to do with them in a Bayesian context and have not seen them used there. So I probably won't add them until I see some more attention devoted to this issue (either from myself or from other researchers).

Ed
